title: REQ-106's env-propagation mechanism is factually wrong: writing ANICCA_INSTANCE=clawrouter to ~/.anicca/.env would NOT reach the genesis loop's process.env
evidence: ~/anicca/runtime/loop/config.mjs:101-141 (loadConfig): parses $ANICCA_HOME/.env text into a LOCAL `dotenvValues` object, then copies ONLY a fixed allowlist of named keys (the DEFAULTS set, plus ANICCA_HOME, ANICCA_WALLET_ADDRESS, ANICCA_BALANCE_OVERRIDE, ANICCA_EARN_SKILL, EARN_LEDGER, CLAUDE_BIN) into a separate `config` object. It never writes back into `process.env`. A brand-new key like ANICCA_INSTANCE, not in that allowlist, is silently dropped by loadConfig — it never becomes part of `config` and never reaches `process.env`.

Confirmed via grep across all of ~/anicca/runtime/loop/*.mjs: zero matches for `process.env[`, `Object.assign(process.env`, or `process.env.KEY =` — there is NO code path anywhere in this directory that copies parsed dotenv values back into the real process.env.

~/anicca/runtime/loop/index.mjs:439-461 (buildSkillEnv): `const base = scrub(process.env)` reads the REAL OS-level process.env of the running node process directly (not the `config` object). Only `config.EARN_LEDGER` is explicitly re-injected into the child env (`...(config.EARN_LEDGER ? {EARN_LEDGER: config.EARN_LEDGER} : {})`); no other config field, and nothing that would carry a new ANICCA_INSTANCE key, is re-injected this way.

The genesis loop actually running on this machine right now is `com.anicca.daemon` (confirmed via `launchctl list` -> `740\t0\tcom.anicca.daemon`, i.e. currently loaded/running), with ANICCA_HOME=/Users/anicca/.anicca. Its REAL process.env comes from the STATIC XML <key>EnvironmentVariables</key> dict inside ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.anicca.daemon.plist (confirmed via `plutil -convert xml1 -o -`): ANICCA_FREE_MODEL, ANICCA_FUNDED_MODEL, ANICCA_HOME, ANICCA_LEAN_MODEL, ANICCA_REPO, BASE_RPC_URL, COMPUTE_RESERVE_USDC, HOME, PATH, YIELD_MIN_DEPLOY_USDC. ANICCA_INSTANCE is not in this list, and this plist dict is NOT dynamically populated from ~/.anicca/.env's text at all — it is a separate, static file.

~/anicca/runtime/anicca-daemon.sh (the daemon's actual ProgramArguments entrypoint, exec'd by launchd) does not source or export ~/.anicca/.env anywhere (no `source .env` / `set -a` pattern found by grep) — it only explicitly exports ANICCA_HOME, OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANICCA_WALLET_ADDRESS.

Net effect: simply writing a new line into ~/.anicca/.env (as REQ-106/Ground Truth literally describes: 'if the genesis loop PROCESS itself has ANICCA_INSTANCE=clawrouter set in ITS OWN environment (e.g. loaded from its own .env)') does NOT set it in ITS OWN environment — because nothing loads that .env's arbitrary keys into process.env. The claim '...it passes through scrub(process.env) unchanged... No code change needed in the genesis loop for env propagation — only a config/env-provisioning step' is not supported by the actual code; the .env-file route as described simply does not work.
why_it_matters: REQ-106 is the single most load-bearing requirement in this spec (per the reviewer's own framing) — if it is satisfied by 'documenting the exact file+line to set', but the documented mechanism is wrong, the whole provisioning plan for making the genesis loop pick up ANICCA_INSTANCE=clawrouter does not work as designed. An implementer following REQ-106 literally would write to ~/.anicca/.env, believe (incorrectly) that this suffices, and REQ-107's live E2E would only pass because the implementer manually `export ANICCA_INSTANCE=clawrouter` in their own shell before invoking run.sh directly — NOT because of anything the genesis loop process itself would inherit. That silently fails to prove what REQ-106 claims to prove.
actual_mechanisms_that_would_work: (a) Add ANICCA_INSTANCE as a literal new key inside com.anicca.daemon.plist's <key>EnvironmentVariables</key> dict, then `launchctl unload` + `launchctl load` (or `launchctl kickstart -k`) so launchd re-reads the plist. This genuinely requires ZERO changes to any .mjs file (matches the spirit of 'no code change to runtime/loop'), but it is a DIFFERENT file (the launchd plist, not ~/.anicca/.env) than the one REQ-106 names, and the spec should say so explicitly, plus note the required launchctl reload step.

(b) Alternatively, add an explicit line to config.mjs (`config.ANICCA_INSTANCE = processEnv.ANICCA_INSTANCE ?? dotenvValues.ANICCA_INSTANCE ?? undefined;`) and inject it in index.mjs's buildSkillEnv the same way EARN_LEDGER is injected — but this IS a code change to runtime/loop/index.mjs, directly contradicting REQ-106's explicit 'WITHOUT any change to runtime/loop/index.mjs itself' and the Verification Architecture Gate's criterion (b) ('zero modification to any already-shipped file ... runtime/loop/index.mjs').
recommendation: Rewrite REQ-106 and the Ground Truth paragraph to name the ACTUAL file (com.anicca.daemon.plist's EnvironmentVariables dict, or anicca-daemon.sh if a script-export approach is preferred) rather than '~/.anicca/.env', and add the required `launchctl unload && launchctl load` (or equivalent) reload step as part of what REQ-106 documents/verifies. If the team instead wants the .env-file route to genuinely work, REQ-106 must honestly state that it requires a small, explicit code change to config.mjs + index.mjs (mirroring EARN_LEDGER) and the Gate's 'zero modification to runtime/loop/index.mjs' criterion must be revised accordingly — the spec cannot claim both 'no code change' AND 'works via .env' simultaneously, because neither the current code nor the current daemon plist supports that combination.
